Welcome to Thornhill Primary School
Thornhill Primary School
At Thornhill Primary School, we are committed to creating a positive, safe and stimulating environment where every child feels valued, supported and inspired to achieve their full potential.
Our website offers a glimpse into life at Thornhill Primary School, showcasing our exciting learning opportunities and warm, caring ethos.
We hope you enjoy the visit to our website, and should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact us.
Together we grow successful learners, responsible citizens and safe and happy individuals.
Vision & Values
Hamwic Education Trust
Ofsted
SEND
Curriculum
Term Dates
Our Vision
Our vision is to grow successful learners, responsible citizens and safe and happy individuals. The curriculum is the vehicle that drives this vision so we endeavour for our curriculum to be broad, balanced and engaging whilst promoting a love of learning which is contextualised and personalised to our pupils.
Ofsted Highlights
Back to School
We look forward to welcoming everyone back to school this week!
Celebrating our extraordinary children's talents outside school!
We would love to hear all about your child's fantastic achievements for our newsletter. Please contact the school office.
Successful Sports Festival
A huge thank you to all of our parents and carers who came to celebrate our Sports Festivals with the children. The learning hero race was a particular highlight.

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) | Thornhill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
Teaching and Learning
Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
At Thornhill Primary school, we teach modern foreign languages in order to provide an opening to other cultures, fostering pupils’ curiosity and deepening their understanding of the world.
In Key stage 2, pupils learn French. The teaching provides an appropriate balance of spoken and written language with the focus being on practical communication. We aim to enable pupils to understand and communicate ideas, facts and feelings in speech and writing. During lessons, children follow the Language Angels programme of study where they are taught to understand and respond to spoken and written language, speak with increasing confidence, write at varying length using the variety of grammatical structures that they have learnt and discover and develop an appreciation of a range of writing in French.
The teaching and implementation of MFL at Thornhill Primary School is supported by Language Angles, which sets out learning opportunities for each
Year group in Key Stage 2. Each year group covers an element of phonetical learning to support the French pronunciation and is followed by three themes per year which build upon previous learning and cross curricular links to ensure deepening on the French language. This allows for progression and retention of key skills and knowledge, and the introduction of some concepts which will support their progression into Key Stage 3. MFL teaching is spread over the year to ensure learning is built upon and given time to reflect on previous learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE) | Thornhill Primary School
pageCache.text:
Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE)
Teaching and Learning
Personal, Social and Health Education (PSHE)
At Thornhill Primary School it is our intent to prepare our learners to be safe, happy and healthy members of the community. We aim to embed dispositions to support our children in becoming successful learners, responsible citizens and safe and happy individuals through developing the character skills of reciprocity, resilience, resourcefulness, reflectiveness and responsibility.
Our focus is to ensure that every pupil understands the importance of PSHE and that we create an open environment to discuss their own health and wellbeing with trusted adults and peers. Each half term, children will focus on a different key question linked to a core value which can be applied in the wider context.
The teaching and implementation of PSHE at Thornhill Primary School is supported by the PSHE Association which sets out learning opportunities for each key stage. It is designed to accompany the 2026 edition of the Programme of Study for PSHE education, which covers all of Relationships, Sex and Health education (RSHE), including statutory content for Relationships and Health Education and recommended content for Sex Education, as well as essential learning on Economic Wellbeing and Careers Education. The Programme of Study sets out learning opportunities for each key stage. This scheme of learning is well planned across the primary phase which allows for progression and retention of key skills and knowledge and the introduction of some concepts at an age-appropriate point. PSHE education will be provided to all children within our school and will be taught on a weekly basis, with some content also being taught through other subject areas, and within other contexts, such as key stage assemblies, ‘circle time’ or ‘safe and happy assemblies’. In addition, we promote British Values through our spiritual, moral, social and cultural education which permeates through the curriculum offer and supports the development of the ‘whole child’.

Spitfire Club
School Clubs
Spitfire Club
Spitfire Club offers a flexible service for parents and carers, allowing children to arrive at school earlier and remain after normal school hours.
Breakfast Club
Spitfire Breakfast Club offers a warm, welcoming and flexible service for parents and carers.
Places must be booked in advance via MCAS. If your child has not attended Spitfire Breakfast Club before, we kindly ask that you complete a registration form and return it to the school office. Once this is done, you will be able to make bookings through MCAS.
The club runs from 7:45am until the start of the school day, at a cost of £4 per session. Please note that children must be signed in by a parent or carer each day they attend.
The club is run by familiar Thornhill Primary School staff, who have excellent relationships with the children and know them well, helping to create a safe and reassuring start to the day.
Each morning, your child will be warmly welcomed and offered breakfast, which includes milk, cereals, toast and fruit. To ensure your child has time to enjoy breakfast, we ask that they arrive before 8:15am if they would like to eat.
After breakfast, children can enjoy a range of fun and engaging activities in the hall until the school day begins.
At 8:40am, children are supported as they transition into their school day. KS1 pupils are escorted safely to their classrooms, while KS2 pupils make their way independently.
How do I book a place?
ALL places must be paid for and booked in advance
After School Club
Spitfire After School Club provides a safe, welcoming, and enjoyable environment where children can relax and unwind at the end of the school day.
We offer two flexible session options to support families:
- Session A runs from the end of the school day until 4:30pm at a cost of £5 per session
- Session B runs until 5:45pm at a cost of £10 per session.
Children staying for Session B will also receive a light meal.
The club is led by experienced and friendly staff members who know the children well and provide a variety of engaging, age-appropriate activities, combining both child-led play and adult-guided sessions. Children also have the opportunity to complete homework in a calm and supportive environment if they wish. A wide range of equipment and resources is available, and activities vary each day and week to keep experiences fresh and enjoyable.
To book a place, parents should complete a registration form available from the school office. Once registration is confirmed by email, sessions must be booked and paid for in advance via MCAS.
While we understand that occasional delays may happen due to work or traffic, repeated late collections (more than two occasions) may incur an additional charge in line with our Terms & Conditions.
For further information about Spitfire After School Club or payment options, please contact the school office at office@thornhillsch.net.

pageCache.text:
After School Clubs
School Clubs
After School Clubs
We are delighted to offer a range of exciting after school clubs for our pupils. These clubs provide opportunities for children to explore new interests, develop skills, build confidence and enjoy spending time with their friends in a fun and supportive environment.
All clubs run from 3:10pm to 4:15pm.
Please note that places are limited and require advance registration.
Tuesday
Dungeons & Dragons
Years 5 & 6 Led by Mr Smith Maximum 6 pupils
A creative and imaginative club where pupils work together on exciting adventures, solve challenges and develop teamwork and problem-solving skills.
Street Beatz
Years 3 & 4 Maximum 10 pupils
An energetic music and rhythm club where children can explore beats, movement, and performance in a fun setting.
Wednesday
Choir Club
Years 3 to 6 Led by Miss Jeffries Maximum 30 pupils
A fantastic opportunity for pupils who enjoy singing. Children will learn a variety of songs, develop their vocal skills and perform as part of a team.
Racket Skills
Years 1 & 2 Led by Cynthia - Solent Sports Maximum 16 pupils
A fun introduction to racket sports, helping younger pupils develop coordination, confidence and fundamental sporting skills.
Thursday
Racket Skills
Years 5 & 6 Led by Cynthia - Solent Sports Maximum 16 pupils
Designed for older pupils, this club develops racket sport techniques, coordination and game play through enjoyable activities and challenges.
Football
Years 5 & 6 Boys Delivered by Saints Foundation Maximum 16 pupils
A great opportunity for pupils to improve their football skills, teamwork and fitness through structured coaching and games.
We look forward to seeing our pupils enjoy these exciting opportunities and make the most of the wide range of activities available this term. If you have any questions about our after school clubs, please contact the school office.

Music
Teaching and Learning
Music
Music is a universal language that captures emotions, thoughts and feelings through musical narratives. At Thornhill Primary School it is our vision to ensure we grow successful learners who can use music to help them reflect on their emotions allowing them to be safe and happy individuals. Our vision is to provide both enjoyable and engaging musical experiences that can inspire pupils to develop and grow.
Through appreciation, composition, performance and reflection our children receive experiences that engage and inspire them to express their creativity in a variety of ways. We also encourage children to understand, listen and explore other cultures through music. Our teaching focuses on helping children to develop musical language, rhythm, tempo, dynamics and textures of music.

Lunches
Lunch
Here’s everything you need to know about school lunches, packed lunches and snacks at Thornhill Primary School.
School lunches
Dolce provides hot meals for the children with four daily choices. We are fortunate to have all our meals cooked onsite daily by our Head cook and her team of staff.
Please see the Dolce website for the full menu.
Meals must be ordered in advance via SchoolGrid (this is an app you will need to download to your phone): https://app.schoolgrid.co.uk/login
Full details about the menu options are sent to parents/carers each term and are also available on request from the school office.
All meals must be ordered and paid for in advance. We encourage all parents and carers to pay online.
Packed lunches
If your child prefers to bring a packed lunch, please ensure that it is clearly named. Remember we follow a 'Healthy Packed Lunch Policy'. Glass bottles, fizzy drinks, and sweets are not allowed in school for health and safety reasons. Due to some children having severe allergies we ask that packed lunches do not contain sesame or nuts.
Below are some healthy lunchbox ideas that meet our school guidance and can help provide children with a balanced and nutritious meal.
Simply-Veg-Shaun-the-Sheep-Lumchbox-planner.pdf
Universal Free School Meals
Currently, all pupils in Year R, Year 1 and Year 2 in state funded schools in England are entitled to a free school meal (UIFSM). All children get free school meals if they are in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2. If you apply (which only takes 5 minutes!) we get £1345 per child from the Government to make school life even better.
Free School Meals
If you are unsure if your child is entitled to Free School Meals, you can check eligibility online at https://www.cloudforedu.org.uk/ofsm/southampton/ or by asking at the school office for a paper form. It is important that you complete this form whether or not your child wishes to have hot school meals. Children entitled to 'Free School Meals' will be entitled to pupil premium. Please see the Pupil premium section for further information.
Free school meal vouchers

Admissions
Admissions
Thank you for your interest in Thornhill Primary School. Whether you have child who will soon be starting school or you are moving to Southampton, we are delighted to tell you more about our setting.
Why choose Thornhill Primary School for your child?
We have fantastic staff, quality resources, extensive grounds and a wonderful adventure playground! Children have the chance to take part in a wide array of experiences through educational trips and a wide range of visitors to our school. Our partnership with parents is highly valued and we provide a variety of opportunities where parents can become involved in their child’s education.
Visiting Our School
If you would like to arrange a tour of the school as a prospective parent or carer then please contact the school office to arrange this.
If you are looking for a school place mid-year please contact the school office to discuss this.
In-Year Admissions
If you would like your child to start the school at any other time than 'Year R' you need to go to the Southampton Local Authority website. Here you will need to complete an online form. Admissions will then notify the school and next steps will be outlined.
To read more about our admissions process, download our Admission Policy.
Southampton City Council In-Year Transfer link
What if I am unhappy with the school place offered?
You will be given reasons why a place could not be allocated at your chosen schools. Your child will be automatically added to the waiting list of your higher ranked school(s) where your application has been unsuccessful.
When a place becomes available, it will be offered to the child who is at the top of the list at that time. The waiting list is ordered in accordance with each school’s admissions policy.
You also have the right to make a formal appeal to an Independent Appeal Panel. The decision of the Independent Appeal Panel is final and binding on both the admission authority and the applicant. The decision letter will also include details of how to appeal.
Please see the Primary Appeals Timetable for information on Primary School Places, year R and year 3 appeals for 2026/2027.

SEND - Special Educational Needs and Disability
Teaching and Learning
Inclusion at Thornhill Primary School
The Special Educational Needs and Disabilities Co-Ordinator (SENDCO) has the day to day responsibility to monitor and co-ordinate provision across the school for pupils with special educational needs and/or disabilities.
At Thornhill Primary School, the SENDCo is Mrs Gemma Clair. She meets regularly with parents, external agencies, class teachers, senior leaders and support staff to discuss pupil progress and review provision in place for children.
Part of the SENDCo role includes line managing the Teaching Assistants (TA) and coordinating training across the school to ensure staff have the relevant training to support all of our pupils.
If you have a concern about your child’s learning, this should be raised initially with the class teacher who will, if necessary, arrange a meeting with the SENDCo.
Further information can be found in our Local Offer (below) and on the Policy section of the website.
Thornhill Primary School - SEN Information Report and Local Offer Link
The Southampton Local Offer web page.
SEND Policy 2025

Sports Premium
Teaching and Learning
Sports Premium
In April 2013 the Government announced funding of £150 million for Physical Education (PE) and Sport in schools. This is often referred to as a Sport Premium. It is used to improve the quality and breadth of PE and Sport provision.

Computing
Teaching and Learning
Computing
At our school we want pupils to be MASTERS of technology and not slaves to it.
Technology is everywhere and will play a pivotal part in students' lives. Therefore, we want to model and educate our pupils on how to use technology positively, responsibly and safely. We want our pupils to be creators not consumers and our broad curriculum encompassing computer science, information technology and digital literacy reflects this.
We want our pupils to understand that there is always a choice with using technology and as a school we utilise technology (especially social media) to model positive use. We recognise that the best prevention for a lot of issues we currently see with technology/social media is through education. Building our knowledge in this subject will allow pupils to effectively demonstrate their learning through creative use of technology.
We recognise that technology can allow pupils to share their learning in creative ways. We also understand the accessibility opportunities technology can provide for our pupils. Our knowledge rich curriculum has to be balanced with the opportunity for pupils to apply their knowledge creatively which will in turn help our pupils become skilful computer scientists.
We encourage staff to try and embed computing across the whole curriculum to make learning creative and accessible. We want our pupils to be fluent with a range of tools to best express their understanding and hope by Upper Key Stage 2, children have the independence and confidence to choose the best tool to fulfil the task and challenge set by teachers.
Through their time at the school, the children will be taught how to use, create and express themselves through digital means. Children learn the basic skills they need to use ICT hardware; as well as learning the basic knowledge to write code and simple algorithms for a computer to follow.
Computing Progression of Knowledge 92 KB

Art
Teaching and Learning
Curriculum Statements
Art
At Thornhill, we provide a high-quality Art education that has been designed to engage, inspire and challenge pupils. It is our intent to provide all children with the fundamental knowledge, skills, and techniques needed to independently create their own unique drawings, paintings, sculptures, and crafts. They are empowered to think innovatively, critically and develop a more rigorous understanding of Art, they are encouraged to develop critical thinking and are provided with a safe space to take risk and make decisions. These skills are not only essential to school but are also life skills children need to thrive in and around modern Britain and have a positive impact on the wider community.
Throughout their time here, they will get an insight into how art both reflects and shaped our history, and contributes to the culture, creativity and wealth of our nation. Whilst exploring history, we also make links with other areas of our learning such as Geography, where children can incorporate their local area and local artists. Whilst encompassing the wider curriculum, we empower children to discover great artists that will enable them to explore their own and other’s cultural heritages.
We give the children opportunities to feel able to share and express their individual creativity, independence, resilience, and self-reflection. We want the children to have a natural sense of wonder and curiosity when studying a wide variety of artwork.
We give the children the time and space to explore new themes, new sensations, and ways to be creative without the need to be perfect. We want our children to trust the process, self-reflect and evaluate, trust their ideas and feel a sense of pride, achievement, satisfaction and enjoyment at every step of the learning journey, not just their end outcome.
It is through the children’s personalised experience of art at Thornhill, that we enable the children to feel safe, secure, and happy, to produce their most inspired, expressive and creative work and ultimately learn more about themselves.
The Thornhill Primary School Art curriculum has been carefully designed to ensure children are continuously building upon the knowledge they have learnt previously and have opportunities to apply these skills widely. Teachers use the progression of knowledge and skills to ensure that learning builds upon previous understanding and moves forward. Every year, children are given the opportunity to explore the key elements of our art curriculum; mark-making, tone, colour, pattern, texture and textiles and form. Each learning cycle includes time to explore the skill and relevant artists and to plan, create and evaluate their own creative responses, reflecting their own personalities.
Each child has their own sketchbook, which they take with them from year group to year group, this records their responses to art and photos of any sculpture or textile works they produce. It also showcases their learning from year to year and allows children to reflect and enjoy the sense of pride in the progression of their skills and creative journey throughout their time at Thornhill Primary.

Physical Education (PE)
Physical Education (PE)
At Thornhill Primary School, our intent is to provide a rich, engaging and inspiring PE curriculum rooted in our school values and underpinned by our Learning Heroes. We aim to develop children's fundamental movement skills, physical confidence and knowledge through a wide range of physical activities, team sports and competitive opportunities. Our PE curriculum supports children's physical, social and emotional development, with wellbeing and mental health embedded throughout. Alongside our My Happy Mind programme and OPAL play, children develop resilience, teamwork, confidence and healthy, active lifestyles. By the end of their time at Thornhill, children will have the skills, knowledge and confidence to enjoy lifelong participation in physical activity and be well prepared for the next stage of their education.
At Thornhill Primary School, PE is delivered through the Real PE curriculum and supported by our School Games programme. Teaching focuses on the six Real PE cogs: Personal, Social, Cognitive, Creative, Physical and Health & Fitness, enabling children to develop both physical skills and their overall wellbeing. Fundamental movement skills are taught progressively across all year groups, with each class revisiting the same key areas while building on age-appropriate knowledge and skills. PE is taught twice a week, providing regular opportunities for children to develop teamwork, resilience, emotional regulation and confidence through a wide range of physical activities. We further enrich our curriculum through opportunities including tag rugby, football, multi-skills, racket sports, swimming, Bikeability and dance, ensuring all children experience a broad and enjoyable PE curriculum.

Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS)
Teaching and Learning
Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS)
At Thornhill Primary School we want all of our Early Years pupils to be happy, confident, resilient individuals who have a love of learning and exploring. We believe in providing all children with a safe, secure and engaging environment, both inside and out, that builds on individuals’ needs and interests.
Children will have the opportunity to learn through play throughout the day, as well as experience direct teaching. Learning will be fun, purposeful and challenging. Adults will provide high quality interactions to develop and deepen learning opportunities. All adults in our base are role models for the children and their learning. We will deliver our curriculum through a balance of adult led (group work and carpet sessions) and child-initiated activities.
We understand and value the use of the outdoor environment for all children, taking advantage vast school grounds whenever the opportunity arises. At Thornhill we provide our children with opportunities to improve their gross motor skills, develop their imagination and further sense of curiosity.
Our indoor environment offers opportunities to develop our children’s fine motor skills through a range of provisions including loose parts, small world and creative station. We enhance our indoor and outdoor environment to suit the seasons, the needs and interests of the children and to promote the high-quality texts that are part of our long-term curriculum overview.
We are passionate about developing a love of reading from the very start of our children’s education: delivering regular library sessions, visits to local libraries, daily story times and phonically matched reading books that go home with children daily. We believe that reading opens the door to the world of adventure, increasing imagination and curiosity, as well as life opportunities.
We recognise that children learn to be confident and independent through the development of secure relationships. We develop caring, respectful, professional relationships with the children and their families. We work together with our families, valuing parents and carers as partners in their children’s education.
We are whole-heartedly committed to giving our children the best possible start to their school life, teaching them skills which ensure their well-being now, and success in the future.
The EYFS Curriculum:
The foundation for our curriculum and the children’s learning experience is rooted in the ‘Prime Areas’ of the EYFS Framework: Communication and Language; Personal, Social and Emotional Development and Physical Development. The four specific areas, Literacy, Maths, Understanding the World, and Expressive Arts and Design, will build on these firm foundations and ensure that children are ready for the depth and breadth of our Key Stage 1 curriculum.

English
English Policy at Thornhill Primary School
At Thornhill Primary School, we place English at the centre of our curriculum. We believe that the ability to read, write and speak confidently is fundamental to success in all subjects and in life beyond school. Our intent is to develop articulate, thoughtful learners who:
We aim to foster a love of literature and language, helping children build a rich vocabulary and a strong literary repertoire that supports their learning across the curriculum.
We deliver English through both the Literacy Tree curriculum and a bespoke Hamwic curriculum which use a thematic and book-based approach that places high-quality children’s literature at the heart of learning. Our teaching is structured around the Teach Through a Text pedagogy, which ensures consistency and depth across all year groups.
Key features of our approach include:
Phonics is taught using a systematic programme in EYFS and KS1, ensuring children develop strong decoding skills early on. Spelling, punctuation and grammar are embedded throughout the curriculum and revisited regularly.
The impact of our English curriculum is seen in the confidence and creativity of our learners. Children at Thornhill:
Progress is monitored through formative and summative assessments, and outcomes are used to inform planning and support.
Teaching and Learning
Read widely and with curiosity.
Write with clarity, creativity and purpose.

Geography
Teaching and Learning
Geography
Our geography curriculum at Thornhill Primary aims to instil our children with an enthusiastic and inquisitive approach to the world around them. It aims to increase awareness of diverse places and people as well as promoting children’s interest and understanding about natural and human environments. At Thornhill, we offer a range of enriching educational visits and fieldwork trips in addition to classroom investigations to enable them to develop a deep understanding of the Earth’s physical and human processes. Our Geography Curriculum is planned from ‘Developing Experts’, teachers plan and adapt this to the needs of our children. We also embrace our school grounds looking for opportunities for outdoor learning. Our children will develop geographical skills: collecting and analysing data; using maps, globes, aerial photographs and digital mapping to name and identify countries, continents and oceans; and communicating information in a variety of ways. We seek to inspire in children a curiosity and fascination about the world and its people which will remain with them for the rest of their lives.
To maintain high-quality Geography teaching and learning, we implement a well-planned progressive curriculum throughout the whole school. Focusing on skills and knowledge stated in the National Curriculum, Geography is taught as a termly topic. At Thornhill, we are ensuring that Geography is being recognised as carrying the same importance as other core and foundation subjects as we believe it is vital to not only develop children’s perspectives on the world, but to give them real world experiences too.
The impact of the geography curriculum at Thornhill will be equipping our students with the skills and knowledge to ensure that they are ready for further education and for life as an adult in the wider world.

History
Teaching and Learning
History
At Thornhill Primary School, we want our children to develop an inquisitive nature. Through the teaching of History, we aim to stimulate all children’s interest and understanding of the lives of people in the past. We teach children a sense of chronology, enabling them to develop a strong sense of identity and cultural understanding based on their historical heritage. This allows our children to value their own and others’ cultures within modern multicultural Britain. We ensure that children learn about significant individuals and events in British history, whilst appreciating how society has changed over time. This supports pupils in understanding how Britain has developed and strengthens their awareness of their country of residence. In addition, children explore local, British and Ancient history, developing a broader understanding of historical developments across the wider world. We believe that by providing a range of engaging opportunities, children will develop an enjoyment and appreciation of History, becoming enthusiastic learners about the world around them. Through this approach, pupils are encouraged to understand the complexity of people’s lives, the process of change, and the diversity of societies and beliefs, while celebrating these differences.
History is taught in half-termly blocks across the year, with careful planning to ensure clear progression within each year group. We use the Developing Experts scheme of work to support high-quality planning, ensuring coverage of key knowledge, skills and vocabulary across the curriculum. Learning begins by revisiting prior knowledge, helping children to make connections and strengthen understanding. This is scaffolded to support recall and build on previous learning. Teachers explicitly model subject-specific vocabulary, knowledge and skills, enabling children to embed new learning into larger concepts. We place strong emphasis on developing both immediate recall and long-term understanding, ensuring that children retain key concepts over time. Through this approach, pupils are encouraged to think and work like historians, asking questions, exploring evidence and developing their enquiry skills, allowing them to deepen their understanding of the past.
